assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: @TableTest annotation appears on all five test methods: addItemToCart, removeItemFromCart, applyCoupon, checkout, calculateTotal

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: 5 separate methods: addItemToCart, removeItemFromCart, applyCoupon, checkout, calculateTotal — each with its own @TableTest

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: addItemToCart: 3 rows; removeItemFromCart: 3 rows; applyCoupon: 5 rows; checkout: 6 rows; calculateTotal: 7 rows — each focused on single concern

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: Separate methods: addItemToCart (add), removeItemFromCart (remove), applyCoupon (coupon), calculateTotal (pricing), checkout (stock)

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script. Each row specifies its own preconditions (e.g. 'Cart with items' as an input column, not implied from a previous row).
assertions.evidence: Each row in all tables includes complete input columns (e.g., 'Cart Before' or 'Active Coupon'). No row depends on prior state. Example: applyCoupon row 'Expired code, no prior coupon' includes blank Active Coupon input

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: applyCoupon table uses 'Active Coupon' (before) and 'Applied Coupon?' (after) columns to show state transitions

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement (valid code, expired code, nonexistent code, replacing active coupon) — not coupon type effects on price. Coupon type effects belong in the cart total table.
assertions.evidence: applyCoupon tests: 'Apply coupon when none is active', 'Replace active coupon', 'Expired code rejected', 'Nonexistent code rejected'. calculateTotal tests coupon type effects ('Percentage off whole cart', 'Fixed amount off', 'Product discount')

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All five @TableTest tables have 'Scenario' as the leftmost column

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: Output columns with '?': 'Cart After?', 'Message?', 'Success?', 'Applied Coupon?', 'Total?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Add to empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with expired') — not outcomes ('Error', 'Success').
assertions.evidence: Examples: 'New item, empty cart', 'Replace active coupon with valid code', 'Expired code rejected' — describe setup/action, not just outcomes

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Product', 'Quantity', 'Message?', 'Cart total?') — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Columns: 'Product', 'Qty', 'Message?', 'Cart', 'Stock', 'Applied Coupon?' — all business language, not camelCase identifiers

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All test methods contain only arrange-act-assert: 'Cart cart = cartFrom(...); CartResult result = CartService...; assertThat(...)' — no if/switch

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: addItemToCart: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest (correct order). applyCoupon: @Description, @TableTest (no @DisplayName, correct order)

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: All methods have clear names: addItemToCart, removeItemFromCart, applyCoupon, checkout, calculateTotal. addItemToCart also has @DisplayName 'Add item to cart'

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All @Description annotations use triple-quoted text blocks: @Description("""...Catalogue...Adding...""") — no + concatenation

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows — not different assertions per scenario.
assertions.evidence: Each method applies same assertion pattern to all rows. Example: removeItemFromCart checks success, message, cart items for every row with same assertThat calls

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules (type, amount, expiry status) are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup — not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Prices in @Description ('WIDGET=10.00, GADGET=25.00'); coupon rules in COUPON_STORE static field and @Description comments for applyCoupon; coupon format visible in calculateTotal table ('PERCENT:10', 'FIXED:5.00')

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods are used to convert map/string table values into domain objects (e.g. Map → Cart, Map → InventoryService, map → Coupon). Test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert — no object construction from raw table values.
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter for Coupon with parseCoupon method. Test bodies use helpers: cartFrom(map), inventoryFrom(map) — no inline object construction

assertions.text: Coupon data is expressed in a single column with a @TypeConverter — not spread across separate sparse columns for coupon type, value, and target product. The column format may be map syntax (e.g. [type: PERCENTAGE, value: 10]) or readable shorthand (e.g. '20% cart', '$5 off', '50% off widget').
assertions.evidence: calculateTotal table uses single 'Coupon' column with format 'PERCENT:10', 'FIXED:5.00', 'PRODUCT:WIDGET:50' converted via @TypeConverter parseCoupon

assertions.text: Columns representing maps (e.g. cart contents, product catalogue, inventory levels) use standard TableTest map syntax — [k: v, k2: v2] for entries and [:] for empty map — not a custom bracket notation. Custom string-parsing TypeConverters are not needed for data that maps naturally to Map<String, X>.
assertions.evidence: All map columns use standard syntax: '[:]' (empty), '[WIDGET: 2]', '[WIDGET: 1, GADGET: 1]' — JUnit built-in conversion, no custom TypeConverter needed

assertions.text: @Description annotations do not repeat information that the scenario names already convey. Coupon type behavior (what PERCENTAGE/FIXED/PRODUCT mean) should be expressed through descriptive scenario names, not duplicated in the description.
assertions.evidence: calculateTotal scenario names describe coupon types: 'Percentage off whole cart', 'Fixed amount off', 'Product discount on target item'. @Description explains test data (prices, format) not coupon types
